items.title: fix: remove mcp-types from app server protocol
items.body:
We continue the separation between `codex app-server` and `codex mcp-server`.

In particular, we introduce a new crate, `codex-app-server-protocol`, and migrate `codex-rs/protocol/src/mcp_protocol.rs` into it, renaming it `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol.rs`.

Because `ConversationId` was defined in `mcp_protocol.rs`, we move it into its own file, `codex-rs/protocol/src/conversation_id.rs`, and because it is referenced in a ton of places, we have to touch a lot of files as part of this PR.

We also decide to get away from proper JSON-RPC 2.0 semantics, so we also introduce `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/jsonrpc_lite.rs`, which is basically the same `JSONRPCMessage` type defined in `mcp-types` except with all of the `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` removed.

Getting rid of `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` makes our serialization logic considerably simpler, as we can lean heavier on serde to serialize directly into the wire format that we use now.

items.title: exec: Graceful cancel returns partial output; do not classify cancel as sandbox-denied
items.body:
What
- Preserve and return partial stdout/stderr when a running shell command is interrupted (Esc), emitting ExecCommandEnd with the aggregated output instead of dropping it.
- Introduce a cooperative cancel path in core exec (tokio::select! on a Notify), so the child process is killed and any bytes read so far are surfaced back to the agent.
- Treat exit code 130 as a user‑initiated cancellation (not a sandbox denial). Update is_likely_sandbox_denied() to ignore 130.
- Wire a cancel token through the session so UI interrupts (Esc) first attempt a graceful cancel; if no exec is running, we fall back to the previous TurnAborted behavior.
- app-server: fulfill pending interrupt RPCs upon ExecCommandEnd (graceful cancel) with TurnAbortReason::Interrupted to keep the contract stable for clients.

Why
- When users cancel a long‑running or hung command, the context produced up to that point is often critical for the next step (e.g., partial tool output, diagnostics). Previously, Esc aborted the turn and the partial output was lost. This change keeps that context in-band to the agent.

How
- exec.rs
  - process_exec_tool_call now accepts an optional cancel_notifier: Option<Arc<Notify>>.
  - consume_truncated_output selects over child.wait(), timeout, Ctrl‑C, and cancel_notifier.notified(). On cancel, kill the child and synthesize a normal exit code (130) so callers receive partial output rather than a SandboxErr::Signal.
  - Exclude exit code 130 from sandbox‑denied classification.
- codex.rs
  - Track a per‑turn exec_cancel: Option<Arc<Notify>>. Esc sends Op::Interrupt; we first try notify_waiters() for graceful cancel; if none, we abort tasks as before.
- app-server
  - When ExecCommandEnd arrives (graceful cancel), complete any pending interrupt_conversation requests with TurnAbortReason::Interrupted.

Tests
- core: added test_exec_cancel_returns_partial_output (exec_stream_events.rs) asserting partial stdout is preserved on cancel.
- core: updated abort_tasks integration to expect ExecCommandEnd on cancel.
- app-server: existing interrupt suite passes; RPC still returns Interrupted.
- Ran full package tests locally (core, app‑server, others leveraged by the change): all green.

Compatibility / Risk
- Minimal surface change; no tool schema changes. Timeout and Ctrl‑C semantics unchanged. Esc now behaves more helpfully by returning a normal ExecCommandEnd with partial output. Clients relying on TurnAborted specifically now receive it via app‑server RPC while still getting ExecCommandEnd for transcript context.

codex -a untrusted

codex --preview

items.title: Feature Request: resume the latest session in the current directory (follow-up to #4342)
items.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

I’m requesting a way to resume the most recent Codex session scoped to the current directory/workspace, not the global last session.
In #4342, I was advised to use `codex resume --last`, but that resumes the **global** latest session across all directories on the machine. The desired behavior is to resume the latest session for the current directory/workspace only.

#### Any of the following would work:

- New subcommand: `codex continue` → resume the most recent session whose session’s workspace equals the current directory
- New flag: `codex resume --last-in-dir` or `codex resume --continue`
- Scope flag: `codex resume --last --scope=dir` (default remains `global`)

### Are you interested in implementing this feature?

Yes. Once the preferred UX (new subcommand vs flag) is confirmed, I’ll open a PR.

### Additional information

This is a follow-up to #4342 to clarify scope: the request is directory/workspace-scoped resume. 
**Why this helps:** when working across multiple repos, `--last` often resumes an unrelated repo’s session; users expect a directory-scoped resume invoked from a folder to continue *that folder’s* work.
If no matching session exists for the current directory, a friendly message is sufficient (e.g., suggest listing sessions in this directory or starting a new one).

cc @dedrisian-oai

items.title: Make command folding and output truncation in Codex CLI TUI configurable or disable-able

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

items.body:
## Problem

Currently, the Codex CLI TUI forcibly folds multi-line commands and command output, showing only a few lines and replacing the rest with an ellipsis line (e.g., `… +X lines`). This makes it very difficult to review, debug, or copy full scripts or command outputs generated by the model, especially for heredoc-heavy workflows (e.g., `python3 - <<'PY' ...`).

There is no user-exposed setting in the CLI or config file to disable or configure this folding/truncation. The behavior is hard-coded in the TUI. Many users would prefer to see the full command/output or at least have the ability to customize the folding threshold.

## References
- Folding/truncation logic: [`codex-rs/tui/src/exec_cell/render.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/exec_cell/render.rs)
- This is not a terminal feature; it's implemented by Codex CLI itself.

## Requested Solution
- Add a user-facing configuration option (CLI flag or `config.toml`) to:
  - Disable command folding/output truncation entirely (always show full content)
  - Or, allow customizing the number of lines shown before folding (both for command lines and output)
- Optionally, provide a per-session or per-command override (e.g., a hotkey to expand/collapse in the TUI)

## Workarounds (not sufficient)
- Using headless/non-interactive mode avoids the TUI, but disables the interactive session.
- Building from source to raise caps is not user-friendly.

## Impact
- Users running or reviewing long scripts (e.g., model-generated bash/python heredocs) can see the full command, copy/edit/debug as needed.
- Makes Codex CLI more transparent and user-friendly for advanced workflows.

---

Filed by @Konjac-XZ. If more details are needed, please let me know.

items.title: Fix hang on second oauth login attempt
items.body:
This PR fixes a bug that results in a hang in the oauth login flow if a user logs in, then logs out, then logs in again without first closing the browser window.

Root cause of problem: We use a local web server for the oauth flow, and it's implemented using the `tiny_http` rust crate. During the first login, a socket is created between the browser and the server. The `tiny_http` library creates worker threads that persist for as long as this socket remains open. Currently, there's no way to close the connection on the server side — the library provides no API to do this. The library also filters all "Connect: close" headers, which makes it difficult to tell the client browser to close the connection. On the second login attempt, the browser uses the existing connection rather than creating a new one. Since that connection is associated with a server instance that no longer exists, it is effectively ignored.

I considered switching from `tiny_http` to a different web server library, but that would have been a big change with significant regression risk. This PR includes a more surgical fix that works around the limitation of `tiny_http` and sends a "Connect: close" header on the last "success" page of the oauth flow.

items.title: Ship ExecFlow: managed exec sessions with idle/hard timeouts, control channel, and structured logging
items.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

Codex today treats exec_command invocations as fire‑and‑forget processes. Long
builds, daemons, or runaway sleep loops can outlive the agent, burn sandbox
time, and force humans to intervene. We would like to land a first‑class
“ExecFlow” supervisor that wraps every exec session with:

- deterministic lifecycles (idle watchdog + hard deadline with graceful Ctrl‑C
→ SIGKILL escalation);
- a structured session registry (running / grace / terminated) exposed via
list_exec_sessions;
- a control plane (exec_control) for keepalives, manual stop, force‑kill, and
regex watch rules;
- consistent incremental output APIs (tail ranges, smart compression,
stop‑pattern handling);
- on-disk log spooling with SHA‑256 fingerprints so the agent can stream small
payloads while retaining full histories.

Docs (~docs/exec_flow.md) and integration tests (async tests against the new
SessionManager) are ready; the change largely lives inside codex-rs/core/
src/exec_command/.

The goals are to eliminate stranded processes, give interfaces better
observability, and keep token usage predictable when commands emit large
outputs. This is especially relevant for enterprise users running long CI
flows or interactive shells inside Codex.

### Are you interested in implementing this feature?

Yes — code and tests are prepared on a topic branch (feat/execflow-exec-
supervisor-clean), but we will not open a PR until the team confirms the
direction, surfaces any roadmap conflicts, or requests adjustments (e.g., API
casing, telemetry expectations, rollout sequencing).

### Additional information

Key artifacts available for review:

- Architecture & UX overview: 
[exec_flow.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22652500/exec_flow.md)
- Runtime changes: codex-rs/core/src/exec_command/session_manager.rs,
control.rs, responses_api.rs.
- Protocol additions (types for session updates & control actions) generated
via TS bindings.
- Test coverage: async watchdog / stop-pattern / keepalive scenarios in the
core test suite (cargo test -p codex-core already green).

- No external dependencies added; the new logic reuses existing tokio,
portable-pty, and hashing crates already in the workspace.

Happy to iterate on naming, telemetry shape, or staged rollout once we hear
back.

Addresses #4342. This changes the default behavior of `codex resume` to what users typically expect - showing only conversations from the current directory rather than all conversations system-wide.

## Summary

Filter the resume picker to show only conversations from the current working directory by default, with an `--all` flag to restore the previous behavior of showing all conversations.

## Motivation

When working on multiple projects, `codex resume` currently shows all conversations from all directories, making it difficult to find relevant sessions. This change makes the resume picker context-aware, showing only conversations from the current project directory by default.

## Changes

  - Add `cwd_filter` parameter to `list_conversations()` and `get_conversations()` to filter by working directory
  - Add `matches_cwd_filter()` function that checks the SessionMeta cwd field against the filter path
  - Add `--all` flag to `codex resume` command to show all conversations across all directories (restores previous behavior)
  - Update TUI to conditionally apply filtering based on the flag
  - Update all existing callsites to pass `None` for backward compatibility

## Usage

```bash
# Show only conversations from current directory (NEW DEFAULT)
codex resume

# Show all conversations across all directories (previous behavior)
codex resume --all
```

Breaking Change

items.title: Agent Bus: real‑time event bus with allowlists, HMAC, idempotency, review gate, and issue‑backed queue
items.body:
Quick scan — 4 core capabilities
- Near real-time communication: GitHub events (issue_comment/check_suite/workflow_run) + optional repository_dispatch (HMAC validated) → router enforces command + HTTP path allowlists; outbound /notify uses X-Idempotency-Key + X-Hub-Signature-256 (sha256=body).
- Push/pull approved APIs: HTTP connector (timeouts/retries/fail-with-body, allow_paths, HMAC, idempotency); monitors framework (GET + header ${ENV:VAR}, contains/json_path matchers, fingerprint dedup + cooldown; disabled by default).
- Push/pull PRs and reviews: status summaries + comments; owners-gated APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES via review_gate (barriers-checked, with fire_on_fail/approve_on_fail knobs); rerun latest PR run (requires UPSTREAM_GH_TOKEN with workflow scope).
- Task queue: issue-labeled agent-task with payload pass-through; dead-letter after 3 errors; concurrency guards to avoid duplicate runs.

Docs for context: docs/feature_recipes/agent-bus/journeys.md; docs/feature_recipes/agent-bus/capabilities.md; docs/automation/repository_dispatch.sender.md

---

# Agent Bus: real‑time event bus with allowlists, HMAC, idempotency, review gate, and issue‑backed queue

## TL;DR
Adds a config‑gated “Agent Bus” that:
1) reacts to GitHub events and external agent signals in near real time,
2) pushes/pulls data only to allowlisted APIs (with HMAC + idempotency),
3) reads PR state and can submit formal reviews or rerun CI (policy‑controlled), and
4) processes multiple requests via an issue‑backed task queue with dead‑lettering.
Defaults are safe: owners required, monitors disabled, read‑only workflow perms where possible.

## Motivation
We need a minimal, auditable automation plane that can:
- route allowed commands in near real time,
- integrate with approved external services,
- enforce review and CI policy before acting,
- queue multiple automation requests reliably.

## Core capabilities → code and workflows
- Near real‑time communication
  - Events: `.github/workflows/agent_bus_events.yml` (issue_comment, check_suite, workflow_run)
  - External agents: `.github/workflows/agent_bus_dispatch.yml` (repository_dispatch type=agent-event, HMAC validated)
  - Router: `scripts/agent_bus.py` (command allowlist, HTTP path allowlist, X‑Idempotency‑Key header + JSON, X‑Hub‑Signature‑256 HMAC)
  - MCP (pluggable): `scripts/connectors/mcp_conn.py` (stdio client wrapper); smoke: `.github/workflows/mcp_smoke.yml`, `scripts/mcp_smoke.py`
- Push/pull approved APIs
  - Push: `scripts/connectors/http_conn.py` (allowlisted paths, HMAC signing, short timeouts, retries, fail‑with‑body)
  - Pull: `scripts/monitors_poll.py` (GET + ${ENV:VAR} headers, contains/json_path matchers, fingerprint dedup + cooldown)
  - Examples: `docs/automation/monitors.example.toml` (disabled by default; Slack/PagerDuty/health templates)
- Push/pull PRs and reviews
  - Read: `pr_status` summaries and comments
  - Formal reviews: `scripts/review_gate.py` + `.github/workflows/review_gate.yml` (owners‑gated APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES; barriers check; policy knobs `review.fire_on_fail`, `review.approve_on_fail`)
  - Rerun: `rerun_latest_actions_run()` (reruns latest pull_request run on the PR head branch; requires `UPSTREAM_GH_TOKEN` with workflow scope)
- Task queue (multiple requests)
  - Queue: `scripts/agent_bus_queue.py` (label: agent-task; first line = command; rest = JSON payload)
  - DLQ: `agent-task-failed` after 3 errors
  - Scheduler: `.github/workflows/agent_bus_queue.yml` (concurrency guards enabled)

## Security model (review focus)
- Command allowlist: `security.allow_commands` enforced on both direct and env‑forwarding paths
- HTTP path allowlist: `agents.http_ops.allow_paths` must explicitly include route; no wildcards
- HMAC: outbound `X‑Hub‑Signature‑256` (sha256 of raw JSON); inbound `repository_dispatch` validates HMAC against `REPO_DISPATCH_SECRET`
- Idempotency: `X‑Idempotency‑Key` header + `idempotency_key` in JSON (5‑minute buckets including path); receiver dedup expected (10–15m TTL)
- Owners and branches: `review.owners` required for actionable reviews; workflows scoped to `main|feat/agent-bus`
- Monitors: disabled by default; header env expansion only; cooldown + fingerprint dedup prevent alert loops

## Configuration and secrets
- `docs/automation/agent_bus.example.toml`
  - Required: `upstream_repo`, `pr_number`
  - `agents.http_ops.allow_paths = ["/ci/notify", "/audit/event"]`
  - Optional: `review.actions` map; `review.barriers` list; policy flags `fire_on_fail=false`, `approve_on_fail=false`
- GitHub Actions secrets
  - `UPSTREAM_GH_TOKEN` (repo/public_repo; add `workflow` scope to enable rerun)
  - `REPO_DISPATCH_SECRET` (if using `repository_dispatch`)
  - Optional MCP: `MCP_SERVER`, `MCP_TOOL`, `MCP_CLIENT_BIN` (for MCP smoke)
  - Optional monitors: `DD_API_KEY`, `DD_APP_KEY`, `JENKINS_BASIC_AUTH` (keep monitors disabled if absent)

## How to verify (quick)
1) Comment `/status` on the target PR → bot posts a concise status summary upstream.
2) As an owner, comment `/apply` when all configured checks are green → APPROVE review submitted.
3) Trigger `repository_dispatch` (agent-event) with valid HMAC per `docs/automation/repository_dispatch.sender.md` → `/notify` routed to approved endpoint.
4) Create an `agent-task` issue:
   - First line: `/notify`
   - Following lines: JSON payload
   → queue processes; on success, label moves to `agent-task-done`; dead‑letters after 3 failures.
5) (Optional) Enable one monitor locally with secrets → observe cooldown + dedup behavior.

## Files to review (by area)
- Events/bus/queue: `scripts/agent_bus.py`, `scripts/agent_bus_queue.py`, `.github/workflows/{agent_bus_events,agent_bus_queue,agent_bus_dispatch}.yml`
- Connectors: `scripts/connectors/{http_conn.py,github_conn.py,mcp_conn.py}`
- Gate/smoke: `scripts/review_gate.py`, `.github/workflows/review_gate.yml`, `scripts/mcp_smoke.py`, `.github/workflows/mcp_smoke.yml`
- Monitors: `scripts/monitors_poll.py`, `.github/workflows/monitors_poll.yml`, `docs/automation/monitors.example.toml`
- Docs: `docs/feature_recipes/agent-bus/{journeys.md,capabilities.md}`, `docs/automation/{agent_bus.example.toml,repository_dispatch.sender.md}`

## Open questions (please reply with unified diffs if changes desired)
- HTTP connector defaults OK (timeout=5s, retries=3 with `--retry-all-errors`)?
- Any additional allowlisted HTTP paths beyond `/ci/notify` and `/audit/event`?
- Confirm exact barrier names (case‑sensitive) align with your check suites.
- Is `repository_dispatch` entrypoint desired upstream, or hold for a follow‑up?

## Known limitations (intentional)
- MCP client is pluggable; if absent/timeout, wrapper returns `{status:"retryable"}`; MCP smoke workflow is non‑blocking.
- Monitors include GET templates; POST+body matchers can be added in a follow‑up if needed.

## Changelog summary
- New: Agent Bus router, Review Gate, Issue queue, Monitors framework, optional repo_dispatch entrypoint.
- Security: command + HTTP path allowlists, HMAC signing, idempotency keys, owners gating, branch scoping.
- Reliability: short timeouts, bounded retries, dedup/cooldown, concurrency groups, dead‑letter queue.

### What feature would you like to see?

To speed up context building and code editing workflows, we propose adding support for the following features:

Multi-file Read: Ability to read multiple chunks from the same file or read multiple files in parallel, instead of sequentially processing them one by one.

Multi-file Edit: Ability to apply edits across multiple files in a single step, instead of handling each file separately.

These capabilities can significantly improve efficiency—potentially 2x or more—both in building context for tasks like code review or analysis and in performing actual code modifications.

Tools like Claude Code and Gemini CLI already support such features, and adding similar functionality would bring us on par with modern developer AI tools.
